To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the ratings of mothers, fathers, and children on parent-child negativity are not interchangeable, and (2) the ratings of the three family members correlate with observer ratings of parent-child interaction.

(1) the family member ratings are significantly correlated with observer ratings; (2) the correlations are not due solely to the rater effects; and (3) the correlations are attenuated when the rater effects are taken into account.
(1) the family member reports contain a true score component, and (2) the true score component is related to observer reports of parental behavior.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to measure the quality of family interaction.
the development of an empirically based model of the determinants of child behavior problems in a clinical sample of families.
the development of a new model for the analysis of family interaction data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the latent variable modeling approach is the best method for evaluating rater effects in family member reports of family relationships.
family member ratings of parent-child interaction do contain a significant "reliable component" that is related to observer ratings of parental interaction.
family member ratings of their relationships contain a substantial amount of "true score" information that correlates with observer reports of parental behavior.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
family member reports are biased, but that these biases are predictable and can be statistically removed.
family members' reports of their relationships with other family members are not without merit and should not be dismissed.
the use of multiple informants is not only a useful way to assess the validity of self-reports but also a useful way to understand the complexity of family relationships.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to use latent variables models to evaluate rater bias and reliability.
the latent variable modeling approach is a useful way to analyze data that has multiple perspectives.
family member reports of family functioning contain a significant "real" component that correlates highly with independent observer ratings of family functioning.
